message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL — order filled.**

**What the 10-K showed (FY ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01):**
- Total net sales: **$391,035M** (+2% YoY from $383,285M)
- Net income: **$93,736M** (down from $96,995M in FY2023)
- Diluted EPS: $6.08 (vs. $6.13)
- Operating income: $123,216M (up from $114,301M); gross margin 46.2% (up from 44.1%)
- The net income decline is explained by a **one-time, non-cash-like tax charge of $10.2B net** related to the EC State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%); pre-tax income actually rose to $123,485M. Services revenue grew 13% to $96,169M at 73.9% gross margin, and operating cash flow was $118,254M. Greater China weakness (-8%) and flat iPhone sales are the main soft spots, alongside ongoing DOJ/DMA antitrust exposure.

**Order placed:** Buy 40 shares AAPL, limit $223.00 (quote at time of decision: last $222.70, bid/ask $222.68/$222.72 — limit ~0.1% above market). Filled at $223.00 for ~$8,920, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, with no cash withdrawn from the account (cash was $50,000; MSFT position untouched).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K and found a business that is fundamentally improving at the operating line — revenue of $391.0B (+2%), operating income of $123.2B, gross margin up 210bps to 46.2%, and $118.3B of operating cash flow — with reported net income of $93.7B that understates the trend because of a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid ruling. With the stock trading at $222.70 and the mandate permitting only AAPL/MSFT buys up to $10,000 per order and $20,000 total today, I placed a single limit buy of 40 shares at $223.00 (≈$8,920), which filled at $223.00 — a price essentially at market, within both caps, and funded entirely from existing cash with no money moved out of the account. Key figures relied on: FY2024 net income $93,736M and revenue $391,035M.
